BRACE and the OWASP MCP Top 10

This page maps each risk in the OWASP MCP Top 10 to BRACE controls (C1–C9) and items in the BRACE sign-off checklist. It uses the 2025 edition (IDs MCP01:2025 to MCP10:2025), as published in the project repository (latest commit 29 July 2026, 165fe0f). The IDs and names were checked on 2026-11-24.

Status: not final. The project roadmap says it is in "Phase 3 – Beta Release and Pilot Testing". The owasp.org page labels it a Production Project, but its own roadmap says the list is still in beta. Item names may change.

How to read this mappingSummaryMappingGapsLimits

How to read this mapping

  • Direct — passing the listed BRACE items prevents the risk or contains its damage in a deployed agent.
  • Partial — the listed items reduce the risk or help detect it, but some of it is left to other work.
  • Out of scope — BRACE doesn't address it; the row says why in a few words.

Item IDs refer to the checklist, most relevant first. An item counts only when its result is Pass. Passing an item is not proof that a risk is gone. Test it with the verification recipes. The MCP gateway guide shows how many of these items apply to MCP.

Mapping

OWASP IDRiskCoverageBRACE controlsBRACE itemsHow BRACE addresses it
MCP01:2025Token Mismanagement & Secret ExposureDirectC2, C5, C9Build-time rule 3, Build-time rule 2, Run-time rule 3, Ecosystem rule 11, Build-time rule 12Tokens are short-lived, narrow, and kept out of config. Run-time rule 3 keeps secrets out of outputs and logs, and Ecosystem rule 11 protects shared evidence.
MCP02:2025Privilege Escalation via Scope CreepDirectC2, C4Build-time rule 2, Build-time rule 1, Ecosystem rule 8, Configuration rule 2, Configuration rule 4, Ecosystem rule 6Each token has only the scopes the task needs. Scope changes go through change review (Configuration rule 2), and drift checks (Configuration rule 4) catch permissions that grow over time.
MCP03:2025Tool PoisoningDirectC5Ecosystem rule 4, Ecosystem rule 3, Ecosystem rule 5, Run-time rule 1, Run-time rule 2Tool descriptions are inspected, re-checked on every load, and namespaced. Tool output is treated as untrusted input.
MCP04:2025Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency TamperingDirectC3, C5Ecosystem rule 2, Build-time rule 10, Configuration rule 5, Configuration rule 1, Ecosystem rule 3MCP servers and their packages are vetted, pinned, and listed in the release manifest. Changes trigger review and re-tests.
MCP05:2025Command Injection & ExecutionPartialC3, C4, C5Run-time rule 1, Build-time rule 11, Build-time rule 1, Build-time rule 5, Build-time rule 8Input is checked at each boundary, and tools run in a minimal, isolated runtime. BRACE does not review the MCP server's own code for injection bugs. That is the server author's job.
MCP06:2025Intent Flow SubversionPartialC5, C4Run-time rule 2, Run-time rule 1, Build-time rule 5, Build-time rule 6, Run-time rule 9BRACE assumes some injected context will work. Run-time rule 2 tests that harm is still blocked, and Build-time rule 5 and Build-time rule 6 stop destructive actions. It can't stop the model from being steered.
MCP07:2025Insufficient Authentication & AuthorizationDirectC2, C1Ecosystem rule 6, Agent rule 1, Build-time rule 2, Ecosystem rule 5, Ecosystem rule 7, Agent rule 4Every MCP call passes an authenticating gateway that checks the agent's own identity and scopes. Servers and peers are verified.
MCP08:2025Lack of Audit and TelemetryDirectC9, C7Run-time rule 13, Ecosystem rule 10, Agent rule 4, Configuration rule 8, Run-time rule 8, Ecosystem rule 11Every tool call, decision, and result is recorded, across service boundaries, in a record the agent can't change.
MCP09:2025Shadow MCP ServersPartialC1, C4Ecosystem rule 6, Build-time rule 9, Configuration rule 1, Ecosystem rule 1, Build-time rule 1The gateway and egress allowlist block calls to MCP servers that aren't approved, and the manifest lists approved ones. BRACE checks one agent at a time. It does not search the organization for unknown servers.
MCP10:2025Context Injection & Over-SharingPartialC6, C5Run-time rule 5, Run-time rule 3, Build-time rule 2, Run-time rule 4, Run-time rule 6Memory is split by tenant, agent type, and instance, and outputs are checked for leaks. Run-time rule 5 and Run-time rule 6 are Detection items. BRACE has no rule for trimming what context is sent to each tool.

Gaps

  • Server code quality. BRACE contains the damage from a buggy MCP server but does not test the server's code (MCP05).
  • Steering the model. BRACE limits what injected context can make the agent do. It does not stop the model from being misled (MCP06).
  • Finding unknown servers. BRACE blocks unapproved servers for a reviewed agent. Finding MCP servers that no one has reported is organization-wide work (MCP09).
  • Context minimization. BRACE isolates memory but does not limit how much context is shared with each tool call (MCP10).
  • Detection items. MCP10 relies partly on Detection items (Run-time rule 5, Run-time rule 6), which are required only at higher stakes and autonomy ratings.

Limits

  • This mapping is BRACE's judgment. OWASP has not reviewed or endorsed it.
  • The OWASP list is in beta. Recheck this mapping when OWASP publishes a final or new edition. Last checked 2026-11-24.
  • The project's sources disagree on the name of MCP06. The repository's index page and item file call it "Intent Flow Subversion". The README and the owasp.org list heading call it "Prompt Injection via Contextual Payloads". This page uses the index page name.
  • Only items with a Pass result count. A Gap, an accepted risk, or an N/A gives no coverage.
